questions.question: Tell me about a change to charting you led, and how you knew it worked.

from.posting: translate inpatient nursing workflows into Epic build requests

questions.situation: When my unit piloted continuous capnography for post-operative cardiac patients across 20 beds, nobody owned the charting.
questions.action: I wrote the charting checklist, trained 45 nurses on both shifts, and walked the unit at 3 a.m. to see where it broke down.
questions.result: Charting compliance rose from 71% to 98% in four months, and the hospital is now rolling the checklist out to its second ICU.

sources.master: Led a 4-month pilot of continuous capnography

sources.story: When our unit piloted continuous capnography

questions.question: What did supporting an Epic go-live teach you?

from.posting: Experience as an Epic super-user, or supporting an Epic go-live

questions.situation: During the hospital's 2023 Epic upgrade I was a super-user.
questions.action: I wrote 12 tip sheets on the flowsheet and order-set changes, staffed go-live support on three units, and logged 140 issues to the build team.
questions.result: Most of what nurses logged was about where things had moved, not whether they worked. That week is why I started the informatics certificate.

sources.master: Epic super-user for the hospital's 2023 upgrade

sources.story: During the 2023 Epic upgrade I was a super-user

questions.question: Why do you want to move from the bedside into informatics?
questions.answer: The projects I volunteered for on my unit kept turning out to be about systems and teaching, and that is where I want my next role to sit. I want to move into clinical informatics so that the monitoring and charting work I have led on one unit can reach every unit in a hospital.

sources.story: the projects I volunteered for kept turning out to be about systems and teaching
I want to move from the bedside into clinical informatics

questions.question: How do you teach nurses something new?

from.posting: Train nurses and super-users on new documentation, in classes and on the unit

questions.situation: I have precepted 8 new-graduate and transfer nurses through our 12-week ICU orientation.
questions.action: I tell each of them that the monitor is only as good as the person reading it, and that I would rather they call me about a number that looks wrong than chart it and move on.
questions.result: All 8 finished on schedule, and 7 were still on the unit a year later.

sources.story: When I train a new nurse

from.master: Delta Ridge Hospital | Registered Nurse, Cardiac Telemetry

questions.answer: I wanted sicker patients and more autonomy, and the ICU let me learn post-surgical care that the step-down unit only saw at the tail end.
